subject: general
question:
A proton is projected into a magnetic field as shown in the figure, the direction of force experienced by it is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/add09c9e690e5c1dbe4182713b6684e37260e2fbc3b034748a0ea7cd2e42ab94.png]

options.text: in the direction of motion of proton
against the direction of motion of proton

solution:
The correct answer is __**into the plane of paper**__.

We can use vec F= q (vec v times vec B) 

Taking the curl we get the direction. if velocity is in +y direction and magnetic field is in x direction then the curl of them will be into the plane

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• To determine the direction of the force experienced by a proton moving in a magnetic field, we can use the **right-hand rule**.

 
 
• Point your fingers in the direction of the proton's velocity. In the diagram, the proton's velocity is pointing upward.
 
• Point your palm in the direction of the magnetic field. The magnetic field is directed to the right.
 
• The direction your thumb points is the direction of the force on a positive charge (proton).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/59d096384bbbce8c181551c79f675e91f46c1a070add65510488467a39b06b8e.png] 

 
• Applying the right-hand rule to this scenario:

 
 
• **Fingers point up (proton's velocity).**
 
• **Palm faces right (magnetic field direction).**
 
• **Thumb points into the screen (towards you).**
 
 
 
• Therefore, the force experienced by the proton will be **into the screen (towards the observer)**.
